claims.claim: The Pentagon raised its official count of U.S. troops killed in Iran war operations to 21, up from 18, in a late Friday database update
claims.attributed_to: Pentagon (Defense Casualty Analysis System), reported by Washington Post, NYT, Stars and Stripes

claims.claim: The official wounded count rose to 865, up 98 since August
claims.attributed_to: Pentagon database, reported by NYT and Stars and Stripes

claims.claim: The two added deaths were both noncombat
claims.attributed_to: Stars and Stripes, citing Washington Post

claims.claim: One added death was Maj. Sorffly Davius, 46, an Army National Guard member who died in Kuwait on March 6
claims.attributed_to: Washington Post, citing a U.S. official, via Stars and Stripes

claims.claim: The other added death was an unidentified Navy suicide in September
claims.attributed_to: Washington Post, citing a U.S. official, via Stars and Stripes

claims.claim: The Washington Post reported last month, based on six U.S. officials, that service member losses exceeded the Pentagon's public database figures
claims.attributed_to: Washington Post

claims.claim: Casualties are split into Operation Epic Fury (15 killed, 417 wounded) and 'overseas operations' since July 7 (6 killed, 448 wounded)
claims.attributed_to: Stars and Stripes, citing military categories

claims.claim: A Pentagon official told the AP in July the second casualty category was created because Operation Epic Fury had concluded
claims.attributed_to: Pentagon official, via AP, cited by Stars and Stripes

claims.claim: Wikipedia lists 21 killed and 865 wounded as CENTCOM/DOD figures, with independent estimates of 25 killed and 905 wounded
claims.attributed_to: Wikipedia compilation of CENTCOM/DOD and independent estimates

claims.claim: No Pentagon public release or statement announcing the revised toll was found
The disclosed Pentagon death toll stood at 19 as of Sept. 22-23, 2026, after one death was added
claims.attributed_to: Washington Post, citing a U.S. defense official

claims.claim: The current official toll is 21, revised from 18 in the Oct. 9, 2026 database update
claims.attributed_to: Pentagon (DCAS), reported by Washington Post, NYT, Stars and Stripes

claims.claim: The Pentagon has described the DCAS changes as administrative: two key enhancements to make the data more easily understood
claims.attributed_to: Pentagon official statement, via DefenseScoop and Military.com

claims.claim: A Defense official said the DCAS changes were triggered by an internal audit of reporting systems
claims.attributed_to: War Department official, via DefenseScoop

claims.claim: The Post reported Sept. 18 that at least 22 service members had died against a disclosed 19
claims.attributed_to: Washington Post, citing six U.S. officials, via Military.com

claims.claim: Hegseth called the Post's casualty reporting 'DISGUSTING and FAKE' and 'a complete lie'
claims.attributed_to: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, via The Hill and Military.com

claims.claim: Davius's death was acknowledged earlier in the year but not added to DCAS until the Oct. 9 update
claims.attributed_to: U.S. official, via The Hill

claims.claim: No Pentagon public release or statement explaining the Oct. 9 revision was found
